situation:
You are the human resources manager at WAYFARER OUTFITTERS CO-OPERATIVE, a chain of fourteen outdoor gear stores owned by the people who work in them. The general manager (judge) has asked you for a recommendation before autumn hiring opens in four weeks.

Every worker-owner holds a share and a vote, and the membership agreement they approved two years ago guarantees the online order and customer service team the right to work remotely. That guarantee is why the team stayed when a larger retailer tried to hire it away, and its members are the staff trained to suggest the filter, the pad, and the base layer that go with a tent.

The co-operative has signed a supply agreement with GRANITE PASS, a boot and pack brand, that puts a fitting bench in all fourteen stores for the season. The agreement requires a GRANITE PASS certified outfitter on the floor of every store during open hours. The online team earned that certification in last season's pilot. Nobody else has it, and the course takes six weeks.

The co-operative also hires about four hundred seasonal staff each autumn, and seasonal staff hold no share and no vote. The general manager (judge) wants you to analyze the choice and recommend one course. Recalling the online team to the floor sets aside the remote-work guarantee without the member vote that changing the agreement would take, and risks losing the team that stayed because of it. Putting seasonal hires through the course instead leaves the benches uncertified for the first two weeks of the season and meets the brand's requirement with people who hold no share and no vote.

You will present your recommendation to the general manager (judge) in a meeting to take place in his/her office. The general manager (judge) will begin the meeting by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the general manager's (judge) questions, the general manager (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the general manager (judge) of WAYFARER OUTFITTERS CO-OPERATIVE. Business background is the same as the situation above. Autumn hiring opens in four weeks, the GRANITE PASS benches have to be staffed by certified outfitters, and the only people certified are the ones the membership agreement promised would not have to come in.

You want the human resources manager to analyze the choice and recommend one course, and to tell you what the co-operative owes each side of it.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of the participant:
judgeQuestions: Which course did you rule out, and what would we have gained by taking it?
What would taking it have cost us instead?
